\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بهبود} (behbud)}{بهبود (behbud)}]{\fa{بهبود} (behbud) — an improvement; recovery}

\label{lesson:FA-C374-behbud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to reduce, then the Persian for to grow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بهبود}}
\textbf{\fa{بهبود}} (\emph{behbud}) — \textquotedblleft{}an improvement; recovery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{حال} \fa{پدربزرگ} \fa{رو} \fa{به} \fa{بهبود} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hâl-e pedarbozorg ru be behbud ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather's health is improving.
\end{quote}

\emph{Beh} \textquotedblleft{}good, better\textquotedblright{} + \emph{bud} \textquotedblleft{}being\textquotedblright{}. For health and for situations alike.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بهبود}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{beh} \textquotedblleft{}good, better\textquotedblright{} and \emph{bud}, the past stem of \emph{budan} \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}: a better state of being.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behbud}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behbud}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{behbud}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to reduce, then the Persian for to grow, then say \emph{behbud} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{بهبود} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An improvement; recovery\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بهبود} \fa{یافتن} (behbud yâftan)}{بهبود یافتن (behbud yâftan)}]{\fa{بهبود} \fa{یافتن} (behbud yâftan) — to improve, to recover}

\label{lesson:FA-C374-behbud-yaftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to grow, then the Persian for an improvement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بهبود} \fa{یافتن}}
\textbf{\fa{بهبود} \fa{یافتن}} (\emph{behbud yâftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to improve, to recover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{دو} \fa{هفته} \fa{حالش} \fa{بهبود} \fa{یافت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ba'd az do hafte hâlash behbud yâft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After two weeks he recovered.
\end{quote}

Formal; \emph{yâftan} has the stem \emph{yâb-}. In speech, \emph{behtar shodan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بهبود} \fa{یافتن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{behbud} \textquotedblleft{}improvement\textquotedblright{} with the verb \emph{yâftan} \textquotedblleft{}to find\textquotedblright{}, a formal way to say that something got better.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behbud yâftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behbud yâftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{behbud yâftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to grow, then the Persian for an improvement, then say \emph{behbud yâftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{بهبود} \fa{یافتن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To improve, to recover\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیشرفت} (pishraft)}{پیشرفت (pishraft)}]{\fa{پیشرفت} (pishraft) — progress}

\label{lesson:FA-C374-pishraft}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an improvement, then the Persian for to improve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیشرفت}}
\textbf{\fa{پیشرفت}} (\emph{pishraft}) — \textquotedblleft{}progress\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پیشرفت} \fa{تو} \fa{در} \fa{زبان} \fa{فارسی} \fa{عالی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pishraft-e to dar zabân-e fârsi 'âli ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Your progress in Persian is excellent.
\end{quote}

\emph{Pish} \textquotedblleft{}forward\textquotedblright{} + \emph{raft} \textquotedblleft{}went\textquotedblright{}. Plural \emph{pishrafthâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{پیشرفت}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{pish} \textquotedblleft{}forward, before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{raft}, the past stem of \emph{raftan} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}. Progress is going forward.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیشرفت} \fa{کردن} (pishraft kardan)}{پیشرفت کردن (pishraft kardan)}]{\fa{پیشرفت} \fa{کردن} (pishraft kardan) — to make progress, to advance}

\label{lesson:FA-C374-pishraft-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to improve, then the Persian for progress.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیشرفت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پیشرفت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{pishraft kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to make progress, to advance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{کارش} \fa{خیلی} \fa{پیشرفت} \fa{کرده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar kârash kheyli pishraft karde ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He has made a lot of progress in his work.
\end{quote}

\emph{Pishraft} + \emph{kardan}. \emph{Dar chizi pishraft kardan} — to make progress in something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{پیشرفت} \fa{کردن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{pishraft} \textquotedblleft{}progress\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{pish} \textquotedblleft{}forward\textquotedblright{} and \emph{raft} \textquotedblleft{}went\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عقب} \fa{ماندن} ('aqab mândan)}{عقب ماندن ('aqab mândan)}]{\fa{عقب} \fa{ماندن} ('aqab mândan) — to fall behind, to lag}

\label{lesson:FA-C374-aqab-mandan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for progress, then the Persian for to make progress.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عقب} \fa{ماندن}}
\textbf{\fa{عقب} \fa{ماندن}} (\emph{'aqab mândan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to fall behind, to lag\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{به} \fa{خاطر} \fa{بیماری} \fa{از} \fa{درسها} \fa{عقب} \fa{ماند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u be khâter-e bimâri az darshâ 'aqab mând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of his illness he fell behind with his lessons.
\end{quote}

\emph{'aqab} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} + \emph{mândan} \textquotedblleft{}to stay\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{mân-}). Takes \emph{az}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{عقب} \fa{ماندن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to stay behind\textquotedblright{}: \emph{'aqab} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{'aqab} \textquotedblleft{}heel\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{mândan} \textquotedblleft{}to stay\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian (EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
